title: Thai Green Curry
subtitle: Fragrant Thai coconut chicken curry with green chilli paste
excerpt: The most aromatic curry in the Thai canon: chicken in a vivid green sauce of coconut milk, lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and Thai basil, made with a fresh green chilli paste that fills the kitchen with an extraordinary fragrance.

recipe.sourceNotes: Thai green curry (gaeng keow wan, literally 'sweet green curry') is one of the three canonical curries of Thai cuisine alongside red curry and yellow curry. It is classified as the mildest of the chilli curries (despite its green colour, which comes from fresh green chillies rather than indicating mild heat), with the coconut milk providing the characteristic creaminess and sweetness. The green curry paste is made by pounding together green chillies, lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, coriander root, garlic, and shrimp paste into a smooth paste. Good-quality bought green curry paste is an acceptable substitute for home cooking. The dish is finished with fish sauce and palm sugar for the Thai sweet-salty balance, and Thai basil added off the heat so it stays bright and fragrant.

content.text: Fry the curry paste in the coconut cream (the thick layer on top of the tin, scooped off before shaking) for 2 to 3 minutes until it is very fragrant and the oil separates; this blooms the aromatics. The vegetables should retain some texture; add them in stages by cooking time. Thai basil goes in off the heat and must not cook or it loses its fragrance.

items.preparation: one tin; do not shake; scoop the thick cream from the top
blended with 1 lemongrass stalk and 1 tbsp ginger to make a simple paste
bruised and left whole; removed before serving
Thai basil preferred; regular basil acceptable; to finish

content.text: Scoop the thick coconut cream from the top of the tin into a wok or wide pan. Heat over medium-high until sizzling. Add the green curry paste and fry, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes until the paste is very fragrant and the oil is visibly separating.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 2 minutes to coat in the paste. Add the remaining coconut milk, stock, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a simmer. Season with fish sauce and sugar.

Add the courgette and green beans. Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the vegetables are just tender. Remove the lemongrass. Add the lime juice. Taste and adjust. Remove from the heat and stir in the basil. Serve immediately with jasmine rice and sliced chilli.
